# <span id="aanchor227"></span> Efficiency Definition Editor

Users must have the Location Balancing module in order to access the Efficiency Definition Editor.

The Energy Efficiency calculation allows the user to view their useful deliveries as a percent of their total receipts. By viewing the trend in calculated efficiency percentages, the user can easily notice any month to month differences in operating efficiency.

Defining an efficiency equation in FLOWCAL allows users to manage assets and identify bottom line impacts. This calculation divides the total useful energy delivered by the total energy received. Users can then determine their efficiency level to compare changes from month to month.

Before accessing the Efficiency Definition Editor, users must enable the subtotaling configuration options and enable efficiency calculation options for the location.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Enable Subtotaling">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Enable Subtotaling Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Enable Subtotaling">

<div class="procedure">

To enable subtotaling:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Application** \> **FLOWCAL Configuration**.
2.  Enable the "Subtotal by Meter Direction" and "Subtotal by Meter Class" configuration options. (See: [FLOWCAL Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#Subtotal))

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Enable Efficiencies">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Enable Efficiencies on Locations</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Enable Efficiencies">

<div class="procedure">

To enable efficiency calculation options for locations:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Location Editor**.
2.  Select a location from the Location drop-down menu.
3.  From within the Location Editor, go to **Tools** \> **Info**.
4.  Under **Options**, the select the check box for **Calculate Energy Efficiency**, **Calculate Plant Recovery Efficiency**, or **Calculate System Recovery Efficiency**.

System or Plant Recovery Efficiency will be displayed, but not both. If both options are enabled in the Location Editor for a given location, the System Recovery values will be displayed rather than the Plant Recovery values.

</div>

</div>

 

<div class="procedure">

To configure the Energy Efficiency equation in the Efficiency Definition Editor:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Efficiency Definition**.
2.  Select **Energy Efficiency** from the **Equation** drop-down menu.
3.  Click the **Edit** button.
4.  Under the **Numerator** panel, select all outlets to be calculated. These outlets are the total energy received.
5.  Under the **Denominator** panel, select all inlets to be calculated. These inlets are the total useful energy delivered.
6.  Click **Save**.
7.  Select **System Recovery** or **Plant Recovery** from the **Equation** drop-down list to define those calculations.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example">

Energy efficiency can be calculated as:

(NGL + Refined Product + Residue) / (NGL +Wet Gas)

In this example, NGL, refined product and residue outlets are selected for the outlet energy efficiency definition. NGL and wet gas inlets are selected for the inlet energy efficiency definition.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 535;height: 429;" />

</div>

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Efficiency Results">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />View Energy Efficiency Results</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Efficiency Results">

Energy efficiency results are displayed on the Balance-Meas and Balance-Std tabs in the [Meter/Location Rollups Viewer](../../Rollup%20Viewers/Meter-Location%20Rollups/Meter-Location%20Rollups.md).

<div class="procedure">

To access energy efficiency results:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Meter/Location Rollups**.
2.  Click the **Balance - Meas** or **Balance - Std** tabs.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 702;height: 489;" />

If the efficiency definition selections are changed after initial setup in the Location Editor, users must restart location rollups and re-queue locations to roll up in order to change the data.

You can also view results in the Balance Explorer using the Recovery Analysis View Template:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Balance Explorer**.
2.  Click **Templates** \> **Default Template** \> **Recovery Analysis View**.
3.  Select your location in the tree view on the left side of the screen.
4.  Set the date range.
5.  Click **Refresh**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 703;height: 368;" />

</div>

</div>
